Actions Performed: Inspect 2x4s for warps/knots/defects; mark reject pieces; cut to rough oversized length for batch
Tools Required: Tape measure; pencil; speed square
Fixtures & Jigs: None
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Raw 2x4 lumber (8ft or 10ft boards)
Output Materials / WIP State: Rough-cut 2x4 segments (oversized by ~1in); rejected lumber set aside
QC Check: Visual inspection for warps, splits, large knots in critical areas
Notes: Batch-cut a full week of frames at once; mark each piece with chalk for easy identification

Actions Performed: Cut all frame segments to final length using dead-stop fence jig; cut all miter angles; identify and mark electronics pocket segment
Tools Required: 12in sliding miter saw (Dewalt); push stick; hearing protection; safety glasses
Fixtures & Jigs: Dead-stop fence jig (one stop per unique cut length); clamp blocks
Consumables: Sandpaper (120 grit) for any tearout cleanup
Input Materials: Rough-cut 2x4 segments from S01
Output Materials / WIP State: Precision-cut mitered frame segments; segments sorted by type (standard vs pocket piece)
QC Check: Verify miter angle with digital angle gauge; check cut length against spec
Notes: Never change fence stop mid-batch; run all of one cut length before moving stop; pocket segment should be clearly marked before leaving this station

Actions Performed: Mill mirror channel profiles into all frame segments; mill any decorative or functional edge profiles; run all standard pieces first then switch to pocket setup
Tools Required: Router table (Kreg or Bosch benchtop); router bit set (straight & profile bits); push blocks; featherboards; hearing protection; safety glasses; dust mask
Fixtures & Jigs: Featherboard clamps; router table fence with stops; depth-setting gauge
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Precision-cut mitered frame segments from S02
Output Materials / WIP State: Fully profiled frame segments with mirror channels milled; segments ready for pocket routing or glue-up
QC Check: Check channel depth and width with calipers against mirror glass thickness spec; verify channel runs full length
Notes: Set and lock bit depth before batch; use featherboards to maintain consistent fence pressure; do NOT change bit height mid-batch

Actions Performed: Rout electronics bay pocket into designated frame segment; set pocket to correct depth for PCB housing; verify fit with housing before proceeding
Tools Required: Handheld router (Dewalt 1-3/4hp); straight router bit; router speed control; safety glasses; hearing protection
Fixtures & Jigs: Router sled jig (controls X/Y travel and pocket dimensions); depth stop collar; sacrificial backer board
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Profiled frame segments from S03 (pocket segment only)
Output Materials / WIP State: Frame segment with electronics pocket routed to correct depth and position; pocket verified to accept controller housing
QC Check: Test fit 3D printed controller housing into pocket — must seat flush; check pocket depth with depth gauge
Notes: This is the only non-repeatable step in the frame lane; jig eliminates variability; always do a test pass on scrap before running production pieces

Actions Performed: Apply wood glue to all miter joints; assemble frame using square jig; clamp and set aside to cure; label each frame with batch ID
Tools Required: Paintbrush or glue spreader; rubber mallet; bar clamps (x4 minimum per frame); F-clamps
Fixtures & Jigs: 90-degree corner square jig (L-shaped clamping fixture on bench); wax paper to protect bench surface
Consumables: Wood glue (Titebond II or III); painter's tape (for squeeze-out cleanup)
Input Materials: All profiled and routed frame segments from S03 and S04
Output Materials / WIP State: Assembled glued frame (curing); frames labeled with batch ID and date
QC Check: Check frame is square (diagonal measurement must match); verify all joints are tight with no gaps
Notes: Do not move clamped frames for minimum 45 minutes; glue cure time is passive — stack clamp sets so you can run multiple frames without blocking the station

Actions Performed: Sand all exterior faces; break sharp edges; remove glue squeeze-out; apply finish coat if required; final visual inspection of frame
Tools Required: Random orbital sander; sanding block; shop vac with auto-on
Fixtures & Jigs: None
Consumables: Sandpaper (120 grit, 180 grit, 220 grit); finish/stain/sealant (per product spec); tack cloth; latex gloves
Input Materials: Cured glued frame from S05
Output Materials / WIP State: Finished sanded frame — ready for final assembly; electronics pocket clean and unobstructed
QC Check: Visual check: no tearout, no glue residue, pocket walls clean and smooth; verify frame is still square after clamps removed
Notes: Do not finish inside the mirror channel or the electronics pocket — finish can affect fit tolerances; mask these areas if using spray

Actions Performed: Receive mirror sheets; inspect for cracks or chips; label sheets with received date; store vertically in A-frame rack with foam separators
Tools Required: Suction cup handles (x2); permanent marker; tape measure
Fixtures & Jigs: Padded A-frame vertical storage rack
Consumables: Foam sheet separators; edge protector tape
Input Materials: Raw 12x12in mirror sheets
Output Materials / WIP State: Received and inspected 12x12in sheets stored vertically in rack; damaged sheets marked and quarantined
QC Check: Inspect all four edges and faces for chips, cracks, silver bleed; reject any with delamination
Notes: NEVER store flat in stacks — vertical storage with foam separators prevents edge chipping and breakage; keep away from sawdust and vibration

Actions Performed: Cut each 12x12in sheet into 4x 6x6in blanks; clean cut edges; sort into blank inventory bin; log sheet count consumed
Tools Required: Benchtop tile/glass wet saw (7in diamond blade); safety glasses; waterproof gloves; suction cup handles
Fixtures & Jigs: Wet saw fence set to 6in (lock before batch); push block
Consumables: Diamond blade cutting fluid (in saw reservoir); shop towels for drying
Input Materials: Inspected 12x12in mirror sheets from S07
Output Materials / WIP State: 4x clean-cut 6x6in mirror blanks per sheet; blanks dried and placed in labeled inventory bin
QC Check: Check each cut edge for chips or micro-cracks; reject any piece with visible edge damage
Notes: Always wet-cut mirror — dry cutting causes microfractures; cut all sheets in one batch session; do NOT change fence setting mid-batch

Actions Performed: Pull blank 6x6in panels from inventory; cut custom pattern per order spec; clean and dry cut pieces; inspect edges
Tools Required: Laser cutter or CNC (per shop setup); suction cup handles; safety glasses; appropriate PPE for cutting method
Fixtures & Jigs: Per-order design file (loaded from order system); fixture to hold mirror blank flat during cut
Consumables: Coolant or cutting fluid per machine spec; shop towels
Input Materials: 6x6in blank mirror panels from S08 inventory; per-order design file
Output Materials / WIP State: 2x custom-cut 6x6in mirror panels per unit; panels labeled with order ID
QC Check: Verify cut pattern against order spec; inspect all cut edges; check for silver layer damage near cut lines
Notes: SKIP THIS STATION for standard/blank units; custom cuts are a per-order operation not a batch operation; pull blanks from inventory bin, never cut to order from raw sheet

Actions Performed: Receive LED strip rolls; inspect for physical damage; power on full roll using bench PSU and test harness; flag and quarantine any dead segments; log roll lot number
Tools Required: Bench power supply (0-30V 5A); test harness with alligator clips; multimeter; magnifying loupe
Fixtures & Jigs: None
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Raw LED strip rolls (full length)
Output Materials / WIP State: Tested and approved LED strip rolls in stock; rejected rolls quarantined and logged
QC Check: Every LED must illuminate on full roll test; check for dead zones, flickering, or abnormal color; measure strip voltage and current draw
Notes: Do this at receiving — NOT at assembly; discovering a dead strip mid-build is a major disruption; log roll lot numbers for traceability

Actions Performed: Cut strip to spec length at correct cut line; flux VIN/GND/DATA pads; solder connector plug to all three pads; inspect joints under loupe; post-solder power-on test
Tools Required: Hakko FX-888D soldering iron; fine tip; wire cutters/scissors; magnifying loupe or USB microscope; bench PSU for post-solder test; fume extractor; anti-static wrist strap
Fixtures & Jigs: LED strip solder jig (holds strip flat, positions connector at correct angle)
Consumables: 63/37 rosin-core solder (thin gauge); flux pen; solder wick; isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and cotton swabs for cleanup
Input Materials: Tested LED strip rolls from S10; connector plugs
Output Materials / WIP State: Cut and soldered LED strip assembly with connector attached; tested and verified; placed in labeled ESD-safe staging bin
QC Check: Post-solder: power on with bench PSU — ALL LEDs must fire; inspect each joint under loupe (no cold joints, no bridges, no lifted pads)
Notes: Always flux before soldering; clean joints with IPA after; never skip post-solder power test; use solder jig every time — freehand soldering on flex strips causes inconsistent results

Actions Performed: Press LED strip assembly into 3D printed spacer; verify fit and alignment; route connector cable through spacer exit port; place completed sub-assembly in staging bin
Tools Required: Plastic spudger or press tool; anti-static mat
Fixtures & Jigs: None
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Soldered LED strip assembly from S11; 3D printed LED spacer
Output Materials / WIP State: LED + spacer sub-assembly; connector cable routed and accessible; placed in staging bin labeled READY FOR FINAL ASSEMBLY
QC Check: Verify strip is fully seated with no lifting; connector exits through correct port; no stress on solder joints from cable routing
Notes: 3D printed spacers must be pre-inventoried — print a full week batch; inspect each spacer for layer delamination or warping before use

Actions Performed: Receive controllers from China shipment; inspect each for physical damage; check component count; sort into ESD-safe trays; log lot and quantity
Tools Required: Anti-static wrist strap; ESD-safe tweezers; magnifying loupe
Fixtures & Jigs: ESD-safe tray (5-10 unit capacity)
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Inbound controller PCBs (from China, ~5-day lead time)
Output Materials / WIP State: Inspected controllers sorted into ESD-safe flash trays; damaged units quarantined and noted
QC Check: Check for bent pins, damaged SMD components, missing components, PCB cracks or burn marks
Notes: Always handle with ESD precautions; never place controllers on bare bench surface; maintain a minimum 2-week buffer stock to cover lead time

Actions Performed: Load tray of controllers into flashing jig; run batch flash script on Raspberry Pi; verify each unit flashes successfully; mark flashed units; place in FLASHED tray
Tools Required: Raspberry Pi flashing rig (wall or shelf mounted); pogo pin batch fixture (5-10 seats); USB hub if needed
Fixtures & Jigs: Pogo pin fixture aligned to controller programming pads; TO FLASH and FLASHED labeled trays
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Inspected controllers from S13 (in ESD tray, TO FLASH)
Output Materials / WIP State: Flashed controllers in FLASHED tray; firmware version logged against lot number
QC Check: Pi script must confirm successful flash for each unit; any failed flash goes back to start of queue; never mix flashed and unflashed units
Notes: NEVER mix FLASHED and TO FLASH trays; label trays clearly; log firmware version per batch; always flash in groups not one at a time — setup overhead is significant

Actions Performed: Solder all required through-hole components and pad connections per controller BOM; inspect all joints; power-on function test; verify communication and LED data output
Tools Required: Hakko FX-888D soldering iron; chisel tip; multimeter; bench PSU; USB microscope or loupe; fume extractor; anti-static wrist strap
Fixtures & Jigs: PCB vise or helping hands; anti-static mat
Consumables: 63/37 rosin-core solder; flux pen; solder wick; IPA + swabs for cleanup
Input Materials: Flashed controllers from S14
Output Materials / WIP State: Fully soldered and tested controllers; function verified; placed in ESD staging bin
QC Check: Inspect all joints under loupe; power-on test must confirm correct output on data line; check voltage rails with multimeter
Notes: Chisel tip for any larger pads/through-hole; fine tip for SMD work; clean all flux residue before housing install

Actions Performed: Seat soldered controller PCB into 3D printed housing; secure if required; route any connector cables; place completed sub-assembly in staging bin
Tools Required: Plastic spudger; ESD-safe tweezers
Fixtures & Jigs: None
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Tested controller from S15; 3D printed controller housing
Output Materials / WIP State: Controller + housing sub-assembly; cables routed; placed in staging bin labeled READY FOR FINAL ASSEMBLY
QC Check: PCB must be fully seated; no rocking or play in housing; all connectors accessible and unobstructed
Notes: Inspect housing for warping or delamination before use; print a full week buffer; do not force PCB into housing — if resistance is high the print needs to be re-toleranced

Actions Performed: Pull all sub-assemblies and hardware for one unit; check against kit checklist; place into labeled order tray; sign traveler card before proceeding to final assembly
Tools Required: None (organizational only)
Fixtures & Jigs: Kitting shelf with labeled bins for each component type; order tray per unit
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Finished frame (S06); 2x mirror panels (S08 or S09); LED+spacer sub-assembly (S12); controller+housing sub-assembly (S16); backing panel; fasteners/hardware per BOM; traveler card
Output Materials / WIP State: Fully kitted order tray with traveler card; all components verified present before assembly begins
QC Check: Check every line item on the kit checklist before releasing tray to assembly; any missing component sends the tray back — do not begin partial assembly
Notes: This station prevents mid-build stops; traveler card travels with the unit through final assembly and QC; never start final assembly without a complete kit

Actions Performed: Install controller housing into electronics pocket; lay mirror #1 into milled channels; seat LED strip assembly against mirror; lay mirror #2; install backing; route and manage all cables; secure connector for external access
Tools Required: Screwdrivers; rubber mallet; suction cup handles (for mirror handling); pick tool; cable tie tool
Fixtures & Jigs: Rubber bench mat (protects mirrors); assembly jig or positioning guides if developed
Consumables: Fasteners per BOM; cable ties; foam gasket material if spec requires
Input Materials: Complete kitted order tray from S17
Output Materials / WIP State: Fully assembled LED mirror unit; all components installed; backing secured; connector accessible; ready for final QC
QC Check: Visual check at each sub-step: controller seated correctly; mirrors seated fully in channels; no visible gaps; no loose cables internally
Notes: Handle mirrors with suction cups only — no bare hands on mirror faces; route cables before installing backing; ensure connector is fully accessible and strain-relieved

Actions Performed: Full power-on test; LED uniformity check across all zones; visual inspection of mirror alignment and clarity; structural check for rattles or loose components; verify connector engagement; sign off traveler card
Tools Required: Bench PSU or standard power connector; multimeter; flashlight or high-CRI inspection light
Fixtures & Jigs: QC checklist (laminated per-step); inspection light stand
Consumables: None
Input Materials: Assembled LED mirror unit from S18
Output Materials / WIP State: QC-passed unit with signed traveler card; or unit flagged for rework with defect noted on traveler card
QC Check: Power-on: all LEDs fire, no dead zones, no flickering; mirror: no scratches, chips, fingerprints, misalignment; structure: no rattle, backing flush, joints tight; connector: engages and disengages cleanly
Notes: Zero tolerance for dead LEDs or cracked mirrors — these are automatic reworks; mark rework reason clearly on traveler card; do not box any unit without a signed-off traveler card

Actions Performed: Wrap unit in protective material; place in box with appropriate void fill; seal box; print and apply shipping label; log shipment; place in outbound area
Tools Required: Tape gun; label printer (Dymo or Rollo); scissors
Fixtures & Jigs: None
Consumables: Shipping box (sized to unit); bubble wrap or foam inserts; void fill; packing tape; shipping labels
Input Materials: QC-passed unit with signed traveler card from S19
Output Materials / WIP State: Boxed and labeled unit in outbound staging area; shipment logged with tracking number
QC Check: Verify shipping label matches order; check box integrity before sealing; confirm traveler card is complete and inside or filed
Notes: Keep this station completely separate from assembly and sanding areas — dust and loose hardware contaminate packed units; never box a unit without a completed traveler card
